result.stdout:
Description:
  Ina (IL to NAtive) compiles a .NET application to a native executable without a native toolchain.

Usage:
  ina <assembly> [options]

Arguments:
  <assembly>  The application to compile: a .NET assembly with an entry point, e.g. bin/Release/net11.0/App.dll

Options:
  -o, --output <output>                     Path of the executable to write [default: the assembly name in the current directory, with .exe for Windows]
  --os <linux|macos|osx|win|windows>        Target operating system: linux, macos or windows [default: the operating system of this machine if it is one of them, otherwise linux]
  --arch <arm64|x64>                        Target architecture: x64 or arm64 [default: the architecture of this machine]
  -O, --optimize <blended|none|size|speed>  Optimization preference: blended, speed, size or none [default: blended]
  --runtime-version <runtime-version>       Version of the .NET runtime packs to compile against, e.g. 11.0.1 [default: newest patch of the app's framework]
  --invariant-globalization                 Use culture-invariant globalization so that the executable does not need ICU at run time
  --symbols                                 Keep a symbol table in the executable (useful for debuggers and profilers; not for Windows)
  --no-pie                                  Produce a fixed-address executable instead of one that the system can load at a random address (not for macOS)
  --intermediate-dir <intermediate-dir>     Directory for intermediate files (object file, compiler response file)
  -v, --verbose                             Show detailed progress, timings and compiler output
  -?, -h, --help                            Show help and usage information
  --version                                 Show version information
